questions.question: A runner completes a long race without drinking water and produces a small volume of concentrated urine. Explain how the kidneys and ADH produce the stated urine. Include filtration, selective reabsorption, the change in ADH and the resulting change in tubule permeability.
questions.modelAnswer: The kidneys filter the blood, then selectively reabsorb all glucose, required ions and different amounts of water. When blood water concentration falls, the pituitary releases more ADH kidney tubules become more permeable, more water is reabsorbed, and a smaller volume of concentrated urine is produced. The reverse occurs when blood water concentration is high.

questions.question: A doctor taps below a patient’s knee and the lower leg moves. Explain the route from stimulus detection to the response. Name the receptor, sensory neurone, central nervous system, synapse, motor neurone and effector in the correct order, and explain why the response is protective.
questions.modelAnswer: A receptor detects the stimulus and generates an electrical impulse. The impulse travels along a sensory neurone to the central nervous system, crosses synapses by neurotransmitter diffusion, then travels along a motor neurone to an effector. A muscle contracts or a gland secretes. A reflex is rapid, automatic and protective.

questions.question: After the same meal, person A’s blood glucose rises from 5.0 to 8.2 mmol dm⁻³ and returns to 5.1 within two hours; person B’s rises from 7.2 to 11.9 and remains above 8.0. Explain the hormonal response. Name the gland, hormone, target organs and changes in glucose uptake, glycogen storage or glucose release that account for the result.
questions.modelAnswer: A rise in blood glucose stimulates pancreatic beta cells to release insulin. Insulin increases glucose uptake by cells and conversion of glucose to glycogen in liver and muscle, lowering blood glucose. A fall stimulates glucagon, which causes liver glycogen to be converted to glucose and released. Type 1 diabetes involves insufficient insulin type 2 involves reduced target-cell response and is managed using diet, activity and medicines, with insulin used where required.

questions.question: The corpus luteum breaks down near the end of a menstrual cycle. Explain the roles and interactions of FSH, oestrogen, LH and progesterone, including the effect on the ovary and uterus lining.
